sentences.text: .2. The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing syn. 32/4 measuring 37 guntas of Byalalu village, Tavarakere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka has been acquired for construction of houses.
Preliminary notification was issued on 24.03.2011.
The final notification has been published in the Gazette on 27.11.2012.
The L.A.O. has passed the award on 02.09.2015.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs. 99,15,379/-.
As O.S.No. 585/2013 was pending for adjudication, the L.A.O. has referred the matter to this Court and has deposited a sum of Rs. 99,15,379/-.
The said amount has been kept in FD in the Bank of Baroda, Bannerghatta branch, Bengaluru-83.
.3. After receipt of reference, this court issued notices to claimant and the objectors.
They have entered appearance and have filed claim statement.

.4. Claimant - Munihanumaiah has filed claim statement stating that the property bearing Sy.No.
32/4 measuring 37 guntas in Byalalu village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka was owned and possessed by Chikkamuniyaiah and he being the owner was in possession and enjoyment of the same.
The said Chikkamuniyaiah and his wife Puttamma died by leaving 3 sons by name Puttahanumaiah, Channahanumaiah and Motappaiah.
Puttahanumaiah died intestate by leaving Munihanumaiah and Hanumakka as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate.

Sri. Channahanumaiah died intestate by leaving Munihanumaiah, Ramakrishna, Muniraju, Marakka and Nagamma as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate and Sri.Motappaiah and his wife Revamma died intestate by leaving Chikkamuniyappa, Munihanumaiah, Somaiah and Hanumaiah as his legal L.A.C.
No.47/2020 heirs to succeed to his estate.
One of the son of Mottappaiah by name Somaiah died intestate by leaving his wife Hanumakka and children Manjunath, Chandru and Ssmt. Chaya to succeed to his estate.
It is stated that all the revenue records in-respect of Sy.No. 32/4 measuring 37 guntas was standing in the name of Chikkamuniyaiah.
After the death of Chikkamuniyaiah all the revenue records are changed in the name of his eldest son Puttahanumaiah as per the oral partition between Puttahanumaiah, Channahanumaiah and Mottappaiah.

sentences.text: POINT No.1 :
The claimant Munihanumaiah has been examined as PW.1.
He has stated that the land bearing Sy.No. 32/4 measuring 37 guntas of Byalalu village was owned and possessed by Chikkamuniyaiah.
He had 3 sons by name Puttahanumaiah, Channahanumaiah and Motappaiah.
PW. 1 has stated that all of them died intestate leaving behind the legal heirs to succeed to his estate.

Channahanumaiah died intestate by leaving Munihanumaiah ( objector No. 2),
Ramakrishna ( objector No. 5), Muniraju (objector No. 6), Marakka and Nagamma as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate.

Motappaiah and his wife Revamma died intestate by leaving Chikkamuniyappa (objector No. 1), L.A.C. No.47/2020 Munihanumaiah (claimant), Somaiah (objector No. 3) and Hanumaiah (objector No.
4) as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate.

The objector No. 3 died leaving behind his legal heirs i.e., objector No. 3(a) to (d).
.14.
PW.1 has stated that all the revenue records in-respect of Sy.No. 32/4 measuring 37 guntas was standing in the name of Chikkamuniyaiah.

After the death of Chikkamuniyaiah all the revenue records are changed in the name of his eldest son Puttahanumaiah as per the oral partition between Puttahanumaiah,
Channahanumaiah and Mottappaiah.
After the death of Puttahanumaiah all the revenue records changed in his name.
.15. To corroborate his contention, PW. 1 has produced Genealogical tree as per Ex.P.1
From the document it is seen that the claimant is the son of Puttahanumaiah and Rudramuniyamma.

Ex. P.2 is the mutation in-respect of MR No. 15/2013-14,
wherein name of claimant has been entered in-respect of Sy.No. 32/4.

Ex.P.3 is the mutation which discloses that katha L.A.C. No.47/2020 stood in the name of Puttahanumaiah and in view of his death and death of his wife Rudramuniyamma,
Katha has been changed to the name of their son- Munihanumaiah.
Ex.P.4 is four RTC Extracts in-respect of Sy.No. 32/4 for the period from 1970 to 2000.
In all these documents also the name of Puttahanumaiah has been entered to an extent of 37 guntas and in Col. No. 10 it is mentioned as Pitrarjitha.
Ex.P.5 is seven RTC Extracts for the period from 2006 to 2021, wherein name of Munihanumaiah has been mentioned in pursuance to IHC No. 4/98-99 in-respect of 37 guntas.
Ex.P.6 is the nil Encumbrance certificate issued by the Tahsildar, Bengaluru South in-respect of Sy.No. 32/4.
Ex.P.7 is the Aakar bandh.
From the document, it is seen that the extent of land in-respect of Sy.No. 32/4 is 37 guntas + 1 gunta kharab.
Ex.P.8 is the survey sketch.
Ex.P.9 is the Hissa survey wherein, name of Chikkamuniyaiah has been mentioned.

Ex.P.10 is the no tenancy certificate issued by Assistant Commissioner stating that in-respect of the Sy.No. 32/4 and other L.A.C. No.47/2020 survey numbers, no case has been registered under PTCL Act.
Ex.P. 11 is the endorsement given by the Assistant Commissioner, Bengaluru South that no case has been registered under the Land Reforms Act.
Ex.P.12 are nine tax paid receipts in-respect of Sy.No. 32/4 and other survey numbers.
The said tax paid receipts are subsequent to the acquisition.
Ex.P.13 is the certificate issued by the Karnataka Bank Limited showing that Munihanumaiah has not availed any loan from their branch.

been dismissed as not pressed in view of the memo filed by the plaintiff in that case.
In support of his contention he has produced the order sheet in O.S.No. 702/2014 as per Ex.P14.
From the order sheet it is seen that suit has been dismissed on 27.09.2021.
PW.1 has stated that in view of dismissal of the suit and in view of revenue records standing in his name, he is the only person entitled to receive entire award amount with accrued interest thereon.
.17 . During cross-examination PW. 1 has stated that Munihanumaiah is his junior uncle's son.
He admits that his junior uncle is entitled for 11  guntas in L.A.C. No. 46/2020 and in pursuance to the settlement he is entitled for entire amount of compensation in this case.
He admits that he has no objections for his junior uncle's son to receive the compensation in-respect of said 11  guntas.
PW.1 admits that in the notification the name of Munihanumaiah S/o Chikkamuniyaiah has been mentioned.
He has stated that Chikkamuniyaiah is his L.A.C. No.47/2020 grand father.
He has stated that during the life time of his father, there is no division among family members, recently they have partitioned the property.
He admits that he has requested the respondent to pay compensation, but he has not produced any documents.

It is elicited that he has 8 children namely Gangahanumakka, Puttamma, Sharadamma, Hanumantharaju, Rudramuniyappa, Gowramma,
Munirathna and Lokesh.
He admits that he and his children have not partitioned the property.

.18. From the oral and documentary evidence, it is clear that Sy.No. 32/4 is ancestral property and the objectors 1 to 14 have filed memo stating that they have no objections to release the compensation amount in favour of claimant.
From the evidence, it is seen that claimant has got 8 children who have all attained majority.
As the property is ancestral property, the claimant and his children are together entitled for compensation amount.
Hence, point No. 1 is answered partly in the affirmative.
L.A.C. No.47/2020 .19. POINT NO.2:
In view of my finding on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The reference made by the respondent/SLAO under Section 77(1) of the Right to Fair compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 is partly allowed.

(1) Which of the claimant and objectors are entitled to receive the compensation amount?
(2) What order or award?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The objector No. 3 died leaving behind his legal heirs i.e., objector No. 3(a) to (d).
.14.
After the death of Chikkamuniyaiah all the revenue records are changed in the name of his eldest son Puttahanumaiah as per the oral partition between Puttahanumaiah,
Channahanumaiah and Mottappaiah.
After the death of Puttahanumaiah all the revenue records changed in his name.
As the property is ancestral property, the claimant and his children are together entitled for compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In view of my finding on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The reference made by the respondent/SLAO under Section 77(1) of the Right to Fair compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 is partly allowed.
The claimant - Munihanumaiah and his 8 children namely Gangahanumakka,
Puttamma,Sharadamma,Hanumantharaju, Rudramuniyappa, Gowramma,
Munirathna and Lokesh are together entitled for compensation in-respect of Sy.No.
32/4 measuring 37 guntas of Byalalu village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka with accrued interest thereon.
The above claimants shall have to execute indemnity bonds with one surety,
undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, L.A.C. No.47/2020 which amount they are going to receive in this case.
The above claimants are entitled to interest under Section 80 of L.A. Act.
The amount already paid by L.A.O., has to be deducted.
Claim in-respect of objectors is  dismissed.
Draw award accordingly.
